Subject: Re: Site intake: private cluster for model inference (technical notes)

Hi Jillian / team — quick technical notes based on the inventory and typical setups we've deployed. Keeping this high level so the call can focus on trade-offs.

Nodepool recommendations (starting point):
- gpu-heavy (inference): 6 nodes, each 8xA100 or equivalent (we've also validated 8xH100 in similar racks) — target 10–12 concurrent streams/model instance counts; use separate daemonset for runtime GPU provisioning.
- mini-gpu (batched medium models): 3 nodes, 2–4 GPUs each, used for scheduled batch jobs and retrains.
- compute-only (control plane + preprocess): 3 nodes, 32 vCPU, 256 GB RAM; run API routing, batching services, and autoscaler controllers.
- storage/ops: 2 nodes dedicated for blockstore gateway and long-term backup gateways.

Storage guidance:
- Ephemeral NVMe: recommended for KV cache and model tensor cache. Mount as local SSD (emptyDir with size limits or local PersistentVolume).
- Blockstore for weights: use your SAN/NAS exported as CSI block (rook-ceph or vendor CSI) with gp-block class and encrypted at rest. We recommend enabling LUKS at host layer if the storage backend doesn’t provide native encryption.
- PVC topology: prefer zone-aware volume binding (topologyKeys) to avoid cross-rack volume attachment.

Networking / addressing:
- IPs: allocate a /21 for the cluster to allow pod IP growth (CNI dependent).
- MTU: set 9000 if your fabric supports jumbo frames; otherwise 1500. Verify path MTU through colo.
- Egress: we route control-plane telemetry to your logging collector via an outbound NAT. For model pulls/updates, allow direct egress to Redwood artifact mirror IPs (we can provide an allowlist).
- BGP: preferred for multi-rack aggregation. If not available, use static routing + distributed SNAT.

Security & logs:
- Audit logs: kube-audit streamed to a centralized collector (Fluentd/Fluent Bit) and forwarded to your SIEM/S3. Default retention: 90 days on our side; we can extend to customer retention policies if requested.
- KMS: we integrate with AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault, and on-prem HSMs via PKCS#11. Recommended: run a customer-managed Vault cluster and grant Redwood a service principal scoped to encrypt/decrypt only inference keys.

Attachments: sample_k8s_manifest.yaml (yaml) — this contains example StorageClass and PV/PVC templates tuned for block volumes.

I'll bring a quick topology sketch to the call. If you want, we can include a short check-list for the colo team to validate NIC bonding, switch firmware, and NVMe firmware versions.

- Irene

2) SOC2 checklist: attaching our vendor side. For logs, is 90 days standard, or can Redwood stream raw audit events to our S3 with 365-day retention?

Hi Jillian — quick answers and next steps so the procurement and security teams have concrete items: 

- Backup/DR: we support both patterns. For compliance-heavy customers we recommend warm-standby in a second colo with async replication of blockstore (snapshot replication cadence can be 15m to 1h depending on RPO). Standby cluster can be small (1/3 capacity) and scale during failover.
- Audit logs & retention: we can stream raw kube-audit and app traces to your S3 endpoint; 365-day retention is fine. We’ll add a one-way delivery (no retention on Redwood-managed storage unless explicitly requested).
- Procurement docs: I'll attach our standard MSA and a single-tenant deployment addendum to the Drive folder linked below. We can also pre-share an NDA if you prefer.

Action items: 
1) Ava to send calendar invite for 10/28 10:00 PT preflight (confirmed).
2) Jillian to confirm whether Vault (customer-managed) will be available and provide KMS contact.
3) Dev will produce a short colo checklist (NIC bonding, jumbo frame test, NVMe SMART baseline).

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqX-invergent-onprem-preflight

Thanks — talk Wednesday.
Neha Kapoor
